author: felicepantaleo
body:
Resolves #51644.

`RandomNumberGeneratorService` gives each (stream, module) one engine, seeded with `initialSeed` + stream index, and the engine continues from event to event. So the random numbers of an event depend on the stream that processes it and on the events that stream processed before. This PR adds a mode in which the numbers of a module depend only on the configured seed, the module label and the EventID. It also adds a counter-based generator that host code and Alpaka kernels compute bit for bit. Phase-2 workflows use the new mode by default, so their digis change: they are another random sample of the same physics. The output of the other eras does not change.

### Changes

- `FWCore/Utilities/interface/Philox.h`: a constexpr, header-only Philox4x32-10 (Salmon et al., SC 2011) with no state. `streamId(seed, moduleId, run, lumi, event)` gives a 128-bit stream identifier, and `EventStream::bits(element, block)` gives four random words for each (element, block), for example (DetId, draw). Exact conversions to [0, 1) and (0, 1).
- `HeterogeneousCore/AlpakaInterface/interface/random.h`: `normalFloat4`, four normal values from one Philox block (Box-Muller).
- `IOMC/RandomEngine`:
  - `PhiloxEngine`: a `CLHEP::HepRandomEngine` on Philox4x32-10, available as `engineName = "PhiloxEngine"` in both modes, with state save, restore and `cloneEngine`.
  - The new untracked parameter `seedingMode` of `RandomNumberGeneratorService`: `"stream"` (the current behaviour, the default in C++) or `"event"`. `IOMC_cff.py` sets `"event"` with the `phase2_common` modifier. The other eras keep `"stream"`, because some of their modules request engines that event mode refuses, for example `LHCTransport` (`TRandom3`). In event mode, `postEventRead` seeds each engine of the stream from (initialSeed + eventSeedOffset, CRC32 of the module label, run, lumi, event), and `preBeginLumi` seeds each lumi engine with event 0. With `restoreStateLabel`, the service seeds every engine first and then restores the engines that have a stored state. `restoreFileName` is refused in event mode. The service throws if two module labels have the same CRC32.
  - In event mode a module can request only a `MixMaxRng` or a `PhiloxEngine` engine. Other engines can stay in the configuration; the service throws only when a module requests one.
- `SimCalorimetry/HGCalSimProducers`: the new parameter `noiseTableFromJobSeed`, `True` in `hgcalDigitizer_cfi.py`. Today each stream fills the table of 200000 x 15 Gaussian values on its first event, from the engine of that event. With `True`, each stream fills it from a `PhiloxEngine` on a job-level stream of the configured seed and the collection name, so all streams get the same table. #51644 proposes to fill the table again at every event; this switch avoids 3 million Gaussian draws per event. The test analyzer `HGCalDigiDigest` writes a hash of the HGCAL digis for each event.

### Seed space and cost

`MixMaxRng` gets a 64-bit seed from the stream identifier: for N events with one `initialSeed`, the probability that two events get the same sequence is about N/2^65 (2.7e-2 for 1e9 events). `PhiloxEngine` uses all 128 bits.

| Operation (`IOMC/RandomEngine/test/reseedCost.cc`) | ns per call |
|---|---|
| `streamId` | 10.2 |
| `MixMaxRng::setSeed` + 1 draw, with `streamId` | 81 |
| `PhiloxEngine::setSeeds` + 1 draw, with `streamId` | 50 |
| `MixMaxRng::flat` | 5.4 |
| `PhiloxEngine::flat` | 14.0 |

The Phase-2 DIGI job has 10 `MixMaxRng` engines, and `postEventRead` runs two times for each event, so event mode adds about 1.6 s per event (estimate from the benchmark).

### Validation

20 events of workflow 38434.0 (TTbar, D128, no pile-up), one GEN-SIM file; only the DIGI step runs again for each configuration. Digis are compared cell by cell, with the events joined by (run, lumi, event).

| Comparison with (1 thread, 1 stream) | HGCAL: different events, cells | HCAL: different events, cells |
|---|---|---|
| Release, (4 threads, 1 stream) | 0, 0 | 0, 0 |
| Release, (4, 4), (8, 8), (16, 8) | 19 to 20 of 20, 97.8% to 99.96% | 20 of 20, 86.9% to 89.6% |
| This PR, Phase-2 defaults: (4, 1), (4, 4), (8, 8), (16, 8), reversed order, subset of 4 events | 0, 0 of 592680 | 0, 0 of 293760 |
| This PR, `seedingMode` event and `noiseTableFromJobSeed = False`: (4, 4), (8, 8), (16, 8), reversed order, subset of 4 events | 15 to 20 of 20 (subset: 4 of 4), 83% to 99.96% | (8, 8): 0, 0 |
| This PR, `seedingMode` stream and `noiseTableFromJobSeed = False`, against the release | 0, 0 of 591221 | 0, 0 of 293760 |

HGCAL needs both switches, because the noise table depends on the first event of each stream. HCAL keeps no random state across events, so event mode alone is sufficient. The event-mode digis are another random sample of the same physics: the digi counts and the mean ADC counts of EE, HEfront, HEback, HBHE, HF and HO agree with the release within about one statistical standard deviation. The HGCAL rows of this PR are from CMSSW_20_1_X_2026-11-19-2300 with a clean area of the same IB as the release. The release rows and the HCAL columns are from CMSSW_20_1_0_pre5, with the same two switches set in the configuration.

### Tests

- `FWCore/Utilities/test/test_catch2_Philox.cc`: the Random123 known-answer vectors (also as `static_assert`), the conversion limits, and the mean, variance and lag-1 correlation within one stream and across consecutive events.
- `HeterogeneousCore/AlpakaInterface/test/alpaka/testPhilox.dev.cc`: 4.2 million words and their conversions are bit-identical between the host and the serial and CUDA backends; the normal values are equal on the CPU and within 8 ulp on a GPU (3 ulp on CUDA). The ROCm binary builds but was not run.
- `IOMC/RandomEngine/test/test_catch2_PhiloxEngine.cc`: stream, seeding, state round trip, `cloneEngine`, invalid states, and moments.
- `IOMC/RandomEngine/test/testRandomService.sh`: event mode against the new reference file `testEventSeeded.txt`, with 1 and 4 streams, other seeds, `eventSeedOffset`, runs and lumi subsets, replay with other seeds and stream counts, replay with a stored seed of 0, replay with a module that has no stored state, and the engine check. The existing reference files do not change.
- `SimCalorimetry/HGCalSimProducers/test/testHGCalNoiseTable.sh`: noise-only HGCAL digis; with the Phase-2 defaults, 1 and 4 streams give the same digis, and with `noiseTableFromJobSeed = False` they give different digis.

No PractRand or TestU01 run was done. This PR does not use `alpaka::rand`; the alpaka 2.2.0 Philox does not match Random123, which alpaka-group/alpaka#2737 (merged) and cms-sw/cmsdist#11033 fix.

### Limits

- `seedingMode` is untracked, like the other parameters of the service. The services do not reach the provenance.
- `ExternalRandomNumberGeneratorService` (the service of `cmsExternalGenerator`) does not support `PhiloxEngine` and `TRandom3`, so `ExternalGeneratorFilter` works in event mode only with `MixMaxRng`. A follow-up PR adds both engines to `GeneratorInterface/Core`. @cms-sw/generators-l2 fyi
- A draw in a stream transition (`beginStream`, stream begin or end of run and lumi) still uses the stream state. The standard DIGI job has none.
- The static caches of `CLHEP::RandGauss::shoot` and `RandFlat::shootBit` are thread-local, so code that uses them stays dependent on the thread. No HGCAL module uses them.
- `FWCore/TestProcessor` does not call `postEventRead` or `preBeginLumi`, so it does not seed the engines in event mode.
- With a looper, each pass seeds from the same EventIDs, so an event gets the same numbers in every pass.
- With `noiseTableFromJobSeed`, `HGCDigitizerBase` seeds the noise table from `RandomNumberGenerator::mySeed()`. The interface comment of `mySeed()` does not recommend this use and says that the function can be removed. The service does not save or replay this engine: the table depends only on the configured seed and the collection name, so a replay gives the same table only if it keeps the configured seed of the `mix` module.
- `noiseTableFromJobSeed` has no default in C++: a configuration that builds the HGCAL digitizer parameters without `hgcalDigitizer_cfi.py` must set it.
title: Random numbers that do not depend on the stream: seedingMode event and a Philox4x32-10 generator
